one_line: Agent-native streaming market research that exposes coverage and freshness without leaking paid data.
what_it_does: Registers page tools for research discovery, archive search, coverage checks, signals, and estimates while withholding the underlying paid datapoint values.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the core entitlement and discovery surface: it gives agents structured coverage, freshness, and canonical-source metadata while preserving the paywall, unlike scraping or generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Description frames WebMCP as the fourth option between blocking agents, enabling scraping, and giving away the dataset.
Seven free tools across 49 pages expose coverage, freshness, and source metadata while withholding substance.
execution_rationale: The submitted product narrative and motion evidence are coherent and show a deliberately packaged agent-native research workflow; the paid-data backend itself is not independently verified.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show a consistent streaming-research product and tool-oriented presentation.
Description gives concrete tools, page coverage, datapoint counts, and value-withheld behavior.
impact_rationale: Market researchers and buyers have a real need to determine whether expensive niche data fits a question before purchasing; coverage-without-leakage addresses that directly.
impact_evidence: Concrete niches include micro-drama, African OTT, piracy, creator economy, and sports rights.
check_data_coverage returns silos, countries, years, confidence, freshness, and a withheld sample.
creativity_rationale: The paywalled agent experience and deliberate separation of metadata from substance are an unusually sharp, original WebMCP business interaction.
creativity_evidence: Withhold-the-value while proving the asset exists is the central product idea.
Agent-facing discovery is treated as a product surface rather than an afterthought.
usability_note: Clear research framing and bounded tool outputs make the intended workflow understandable.
red_flags: Underlying paid datapoints and purchase conversion are not directly verified.
advance_reason: High-leverage, distinctive agent-native product with substantial evidence.

one_line: A map whose viewport, places, routes, and pins are directly understandable to agents.
what_it_does: Pairs a human Leaflet/OpenStreetMap map with structured tools for viewport inspection, exact camera movement, nearby search, distance, routing, and shared pins.
leverage_rationale: Semantic camera and geographic operations remove the ambiguity of pixel gestures on a canvas map; generic automation is materially less reliable for exact location and visible-state tasks.
leverage_evidence: Description enumerates viewport, camera, nearby-place, distance, route, and pin tools.
Frame sheets show changing London map views, markers, and an agent-facing panel.
execution_rationale: The motion evidence shows a coherent map application across changing states and the stated central-London workflow; exact tool results are not fully legible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show map views with changing zoom and markers.
Description identifies real Leaflet/OpenStreetMap tiles and a focused demo scope.
impact_rationale: Travel, delivery, field work, ride-hailing, and emergency workflows depend on reliable map semantics; the tool surface addresses a concrete agent limitation.
impact_evidence: Description names multiple map-dependent domains.
Nearby search, routing, measurement, and pins correspond to common real tasks.
creativity_rationale: Making geographic viewport semantics first-class for a visual map is a strong medium-specific interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Explicitly targets the mismatch between pixel gestures and stable geographic meaning.
Human and agent operate the same map state.
usability_note: Familiar map UI combined with clear semantic operations should be approachable.
red_flags: Exact route/search outputs are difficult to verify from the frame scale.
standouts: Excellent fit between WebMCP and canvas-map ambiguity.
advance_reason: Strong practical leverage and credible product evidence.

one_line: A shared image editor where a person and agent edit one canvas and one undo history.
what_it_does: Extends MiniPaint with tools for document and layer inspection, edits, adjustments, social variants, export, and shared undo/redo.
leverage_rationale: The meaningful delta is shared live document state and shared history: the agent sees human edits and its edits can be undone with the same Ctrl+Z, avoiding stale-copy handoffs.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly claims one document and one shared undo stack.
Description lists read/write tools and a sequence where later variants start from the human's current canvas.
execution_rationale: The focused scope and described sequence are coherent, and frame evidence shows the editor workflow; exact agent calls are not fully readable.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show a real image-editor interface and changing document states.
Description gives a concrete photo, Instagram variant, headline, manual nudge, portrait variant, and undo sequence.
impact_rationale: Designers and social-content creators have a direct need for format variants and iterative edits without losing human control.
impact_evidence: Supports Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, X, and YouTube variants.
Human can continue editing and reverse agent work in the same history.
creativity_rationale: Shared undo and continuity between hand edits and agent edits is a distinctive collaboration model applied deeply to an editor.
creativity_evidence: Agent starts transformations from the user's latest position.
One undo removes an agent-created variant alongside human actions.
usability_note: Familiar editor affordances and reversible collaboration support confidence.
red_flags: Built on the existing MiniPaint project; novelty is primarily the shared WebMCP layer.
standouts: Shared history is a crisp, user-visible human-agent contract.
advance_reason: Strong shared-state concept with credible motion evidence.

one_line: A flight simulator that tests whether an agent can fly, handle an unseen emergency, and land.
what_it_does: Runs a fixed-rate STL-to-Chicago mission with route checkpoints, ATC coordination, sealed emergency, scoring, and trajectory export through structured tools.
leverage_rationale: Structured live simulator state and validated commands are central to evaluating an agent under continuous physics and time pressure; generic UI automation would be markedly less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Six tools read the manual, start flight, program commands, coordinate with ATC, and wait for events.
Description specifies 60 Hz physics, real elapsed deadlines, and detailed trajectory records.
execution_rationale: Frame sheets show a coherent flight simulator with aircraft, telemetry, and changing state; emergency handling and successful landing are described but not fully legible in the contact sheets.
execution_evidence: Frames show browser flight simulation, aircraft state, telemetry, and aviation panels.
Description specifies checkpoints, penalties, emergency timing, and exportable trajectory.
impact_rationale: Model developers and evaluation researchers need difficult embodied-agent tests with measurable outcomes; this provides a concrete time-sensitive benchmark scenario.
impact_evidence: Explicit audience is model developers and evaluation researchers.
Scoring covers emergency latency, mission time, G-force, motion, landing, and crashes.
creativity_rationale: A sealed-emergency flight evaluation with continuous physics and agent accountability is memorable and ambitious for WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Agent must coordinate with simulated ATC and respond to an unknown emergency.
Trajectory records tool calls, state transitions, latency, score changes, and events.
usability_note: The simulator is specialized but the mission and scoring provide a clear evaluation frame.
red_flags: Final mission success and emergency resolution are not clearly visible in the frame sheets.

one_line: A banking portal where an agent researches and prepares applications while a human retains submission control.
what_it_does: Provides product search, comparison, profile-grounded eligibility checks, visual explanations, application-basket assembly, and a human approval gate.
leverage_rationale: Private session data, deterministic eligibility, shared comparison state, and safe staging are materially better served by structured page tools than visual automation.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies 15 tools, private-profile eligibility, comparison highlighting, and a submit action that never submits.
Frame sheets show banking login, home, comparison, product, and application-oriented states.
execution_rationale: The banking surface and workflow are coherent in the motion evidence, with a credible human-in-the-loop design; the final approval sequence is not fully demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Frames show login, banking hero, compare page, cards, and iterative interaction states.
Description provides concrete product counts, rules-engine behavior, and approval semantics.
impact_rationale: Consumers choosing financial products face complex terms and eligibility constraints; grounded comparison and application preparation provide credible value while preserving agency.
impact_evidence: 21 products across eight categories are described.
Eligibility reasons, alternatives, and human approval address consequential decisions.
creativity_rationale: Agent-native banking comparison with visual evidence of recommendation drivers and an enforced human gate is a strong domain-specific interaction.
creativity_evidence: Agent highlights exact comparison rows that drove its recommendation.
Final submission is structurally human-only rather than merely prompt-restricted.
usability_note: Familiar banking patterns plus visible reasoning support trust.
red_flags: Authenticated flow and final approval behavior are not fully visible in frames.

one_line: Audits WebMCP tool surfaces against attacks and issues verifiable trust badges.
what_it_does: Lets site owners or reviewers inspect tools, run focused or gauntlet attacks, review agent/tool outcomes, and obtain signed, revocable audit results.
leverage_rationale: Testing the structured agent-tool boundary is the product itself; ordinary UI automation cannot expose and exercise the same contract, metadata, output, and policy surface comparably.
leverage_evidence: Frames show an agent-security dashboard with test and gauntlet flows.
Description covers tool descriptions, outputs, attacks, findings, signatures, and revocation.
execution_rationale: The motion evidence shows a consistent branded audit console progressing from readiness to testing and results; complete signed-report verification is not legible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show ready-to-test, execution, and result views.
Description and packaging agree on the trust-audit concept and live service.
impact_rationale: Agent-facing tool security is a specific and consequential adoption problem, and adversarial testing plus proof directly addresses trust before agents act.
impact_evidence: Targets prompt injection in tool descriptions/results and mislabeled state-changing tools.
Signed, offline-verifiable badges communicate audit status to downstream users.
creativity_rationale: Combining a live attack range with signed, revocable trust artifacts is a memorable and technically ambitious WebMCP safety product.
creativity_evidence: Eight tool-surface attacks are framed as a scored range.
Badge issuance and offline signature verification extend beyond a conventional dashboard.
usability_note: Security findings and a scored range make the complex trust problem legible.
red_flags: Cryptographic verification details are claimed more strongly than visibly demonstrated.
standouts: Directly addresses the new WebMCP trust boundary.

one_line: An adaptive quiz workspace built live by the user's existing AI through WebMCP.
what_it_does: An agent creates quizzes and study plans; the page grades deterministically, exposes misses and topic accuracy, and supports targeted explanations and new questions.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP creates a shared learning loop: the agent builds content and reads structured performance while the learner answers directly in the page, which is more reliable than transcript handoff.
leverage_evidence: Agent creates sessions and reads misses, topic accuracy, and flagged cards.
The page performs deterministic grading and renders targeted adaptation.
execution_rationale: The claimed workflow is unusually complete and the frame sheets show a coherent quiz product progression, though exact adaptive calls are not fully legible.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets and a live demo are supplied.
Description covers build, answer, grade, inspect, adapt, mastery, summary, and manual fallback.
impact_rationale: Students preparing for exams have a clear need for low-friction personalized practice, and using an AI they already have reduces setup and backend burden.
impact_evidence: Specific student/exam audience and weak-topic targeting are explicit.
Multilingual testing and deterministic grading support credible value.
creativity_rationale: The interaction model—agent constructs, learner answers on-page, page grades, agent adapts from structured misses—is a strong synthesis with clear pedagogical intent.
creativity_evidence: Agent content generation is separated from deterministic assessment.
Agent-ready, tools-blocked, and manual modes provide graceful degradation.
usability_note: The answer-and-feedback loop is familiar, with clear progress and fallback modes.
red_flags: Quality of generated explanations is not independently evaluated.
standouts: Strong end-to-end educational loop without a backend AI.
advance_reason: Clear audience value and coherent shared-state workflow.

one_line: An agent-visible icon library for searching, restyling, curating, and exporting consistent icon sets.
what_it_does: Provides 337,000+ open-source icons with page-local tools for search, filters, size/color/stroke changes, collections, and multi-format export.
leverage_rationale: Structured page-local discovery and styling solve the agent's icon-site interaction problem better than inventing SVGs or scraping, but a general agent can approximate much of the outcome with friction.
leverage_evidence: Description lists search/filter, restyle, code reading, download, and collection tools.
Frames show icon-library/search/styling states and visible agent-oriented interactions.
execution_rationale: The motion evidence and product description are coherent and show a substantial, focused library workflow; full export completion is not clearly visible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show consistent icon browsing and styling UI.
Description gives the library size, source sets, 16 tools, and export formats.
impact_rationale: App developers and designers have a recurring need for consistent reusable icons and exact export formats, especially when agents otherwise invent or mix assets.
impact_evidence: 337,000+ icons from 239 sets are described.
Exports include SVG, React, Vue, Svelte, SwiftUI, Xcode assets, and PNG.
creativity_rationale: A useful and memorable application of WebMCP to a visual asset library, though the underlying icon-library category is established.
creativity_evidence: The human can art-direct while the agent searches and restyles the same page.
Agent access is offered both through the site's tools and an editor MCP server.
usability_note: Large library, familiar controls, and broad export support fit the target workflow.
red_flags: The core icon library predates the challenge; WebMCP is an incremental release feature.
standouts: Practical agent access to a large, coherent asset catalog.
advance_reason: Strong utility and evidence, with more incremental novelty than the top projects.

one_line: A shared 3D planning board where humans and agents delegate work to specialist agents.
what_it_does: Maintains a persistent plan, supports status changes and delegation to seven specialists, and renders the event stream as a live 3D scene.
leverage_rationale: Shared server-backed board state, delegation, and returned results create meaningful human-agent coordination; ordinary UI driving would be less reliable for concurrent task state, though 3D is not essential.
leverage_evidence: Description says page tools write the same persistent board as the human UI.
Seven specialists are routed from board items and results land back on those items.
execution_rationale: Frame sheets show a coherent 3D workspace and the described lifecycle is intentional; backend persistence and completed specialist results are not fully visible.
execution_evidence: Frames show the shared 3D/canvas presentation across product states.
Description specifies todo-doing-done, delegation, returned results, and live rendering.
impact_rationale: Individuals and teams managing complex work can benefit from persistent planning and specialist delegation, though the evidence does not establish broad operational depth.
impact_evidence: Clear planning/delegation audience and workflow.
Results attach back to actionable plan items rather than remaining in chat.
creativity_rationale: The event stream as a 3D world and specialist-agent team make an original collaborative interaction for a planning product.
creativity_evidence: Board items orbit as labeled motes and beams show routing.
Visualization is claimed to render the same event stream as the shared state.
usability_note: The visual metaphor is memorable but may be denser than a conventional board.
red_flags: Specialist execution and persistent backend behavior are not fully observable in frames.
standouts: Strong visual treatment of shared agent state.
advance_reason: Distinctive collaborative planning concept with credible product evidence.

one_line: A shared character forge that turns generated art into consistent, editable character packs.
what_it_does: Inspects character workspaces, validates and normalizes assets, preserves protected pixels, checks revisions and hashes, stitches layers deterministically, and exports editable packs and texture atlases.
leverage_rationale: Structured asset contracts, source hashes, revision checks, protected pixels, and deterministic stitching give agents reliable character-production capabilities unavailable through screenshot-driven UI manipulation.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly contrasts exact workspace state and contracts with screenshot guessing.
Frame sheets show a character-forge UI with layer/asset-oriented states and agent-assisted production.
execution_rationale: The product scope is coherent and the motion evidence establishes a substantial character workspace; exact validation and export results are not fully legible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show consistent character, layer, and forge states.
Description gives concrete validation, normalization, deterministic stitching, undo/redo, duplication, and export behavior.
impact_rationale: Character designers, game creators, storytellers, and avatar builders have a real need for consistent multi-asset character production rather than one-off generations.
impact_evidence: Addresses drift in pose, scale, alignment, transparency, and identity.
Exports editable sources and a lossless WebP texture atlas.
creativity_rationale: A human-reviewed, agent-operated character production pipeline with technical asset guarantees is an ambitious and distinctive use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Treats generated character art as a reusable structured pack rather than isolated images.
Combines creative direction with deterministic production constraints.
usability_note: Powerful workflow, though the asset-contract details may be complex for casual creators.
red_flags: Technical validation and lossless export claims are not independently verified from the frames.
standouts: WebMCP is tightly matched to structured creative asset production.
advance_reason: High leverage and originality with a concrete creative-production audience.
